_about: Agent roles: which agent does each job, and how it must be dispatched. Shipped defaults.
A role names a job, not an agent. 'providers' is an ordered preference list; the first one installed is used.
Dispatch by role with subagent_type 'role:<role>', or 'role:<job>:<role>' from a team job (for example role:refactor:engineer); or by the agent's own name, and the rules below still apply.

Resolution order (docs/PROJECT-TEAM.md, "Roles"): the repo binding's 'roles', then _personal/agent-roles.json, then this file. At each level the key '<job>:<role>' is tried before '<role>'. A level naming only agents that are not installed is skipped and logged.

When no level matches, a review role (reviewer, code-review) goes to the built-in general-purpose agent, never to the session that did the work. Any other role is denied, and the session does the work itself.
Put an owner- or employer-specific provider in _personal/agent-roles.json, never here: this file is published.
Enforced by runtime/agent-roles.py (PreToolUse on Agent, SubagentStop), using runtime/team_roles.py. Edit the tables, not the hook.
model: forced on every dispatch of the role. Put [model-approved] in the dispatch description to keep a different model for one dispatch.
nested_model: ceiling for agents the role's agent spawns itself (opus, or no model given, is lowered to this).

prompt_append: added to the dispatch prompt once; {reviews} in it becomes the binding's 'reviews' folder (default axis/runs/). run_record: the agent may not stop until it has written a record folder under the binding's 'reviews' (default axis/runs/).
